title: Kernel arbitration & capture stabilization for heterogeneous-batch CUDA graphs
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Intermittent OOMs and incorrect token ordering have been traced to non-deterministic kernel binding and capture jitter when CUDA graphs are created concurrently for heterogeneous prefill batch sizes across multiple decode streams. This ticket implements an arbitration layer and stabilization heuristics to make graph capture deterministic and to ensure replay correctness across varying batch shapes and attention modes.
acceptance_criteria: Replays for mixed-batch prefill+decode workloads are deterministic across 1000 consecutive capture/replay iterations on a T4 and an A100 cluster under load
No observed ordering regressions (token interleaving) in the canary prompt suite (regression set: 120 prompt variants) after stabilization heuristics are enabled
End-to-end p50 latency for standard chat workload degrades by < 5% and throughput remains within SLA compared to baseline with graphs disabled
Automated gating tests added to CI that reproduce previously flaky interleaved-capture failure and now pass consistently
design_decisions: Introduce a Kernel Arbitration Table (KAT) that assigns stable affinity keys to kernel launches during capture based on stream id, prefill-length, and attention-mode metadata

Prefer sticky kernel-mapping: once a kernel affinity is chosen for a (model, attention-mode, sequence-length bucket) tuple, subsequent captures in the same runtime epoch reuse the mapping to prevent capture churn
Add a lightweight capture fencing mechanism to ensure prefill phase completes KV-cache flush and prefix anchors before decode graph capture begins
Trade-off: small increase in memory footprint for KAT metadata in exchange for determinism. KAT TTL cycles to prevent stale mappings from accumulating
Maintain path for legacy behavior via runtime flag `--cuda-graph-relaxed-capture` for rolling canaries and long tail investigations
progress_updates: 2025-02-20: Ticket created after triage with perf team. Initial investigation reproduces failure with deterministic jitter tool (reproduction harness attached).
2025-02-24: PoC KAT implemented in runtime layer; local unit tests show elimination of one class of non-deterministic kernel binding on devbox. Branch: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1874

2025-02-27: Bench portal run: mixed-batch (1,4,8) prefill + decode workload on A100. Baseline p50 token latency 38ms, KAT-enabled p50 39.2ms (+3.2%). Throughput within SLA. Dashboard: internal.board/bench/ENG-68213
2025-03-02: Added capture fencing and KV-anchor handshake. Reproduced previously failing interleaved-capture case 0/1000 after changes.
testing_plan: Unit tests for KAT insertion/removal, edge cases for TTL expiry and mapping collisions
Integration test harness: multi-stream replay with controlled jitter across CPU/GPU scheduling to validate determinism (1000 iterations)
Stress test on preemptible cluster to surface race windows introduced by autoscaler and driver preemption
Add CI gating job that runs a minimal mixed-batch regression suite on a pinned GPU to catch regressions early
Smoke tests of `--cuda-graph-relaxed-capture` to ensure rollback path functions and metrics emitted
benchmarks: A100 mixed-batch end-to-end: baseline p50=38ms, KAT+prefs p50=39.2ms (+3.2%), p95 delta +4.8%
T4 heavy-tail: baseline p95=210ms, KAT-enabled p95=215ms (+2.4%)
Memory overhead: KAT metadata ~0.6% of GPU reserved RAM in stressed run (peak)
Correctness: regression suite token-order failures: baseline 14/120, KAT-enabled 0/120
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: KAT metadata growth under long-lived VMs could cause increased host memory pressure. Mitigation: TTL and periodic compaction job, limit per-model entries
Risk: Sticky kernel mapping may mask true suboptimal kernel choice for new sequence-length distributions. Mitigation: background re-evaluation job that proposes remapping windows during low traffic
Risk: Interaction with Dedicated autoscaler causing capture windows to align. Mitigation: introduce random small capture jitter when autoscaler activity is detected and monitor regressions
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (canary): enable KAT + fencing on 5% of hosted API traffic behind runtime flag, monitor correctness and cost metrics for 72h
Stage 2 (ramp): increase to 50% with observability hooks and QA signoff after 7 days
Stage 3 (gradual): default-on for all hosted clusters and included in runtime-1.20 unless rollback triggers fires
Rollback: runtime flag `--cuda-graph-relaxed-capture` and hotfix branch available; automated rollback if token-order regressions > 0.1% or latency degradation > 10%

We should coordinate with Dedicated infra to reserve small burst headroom for fenced capture windows to avoid spurious preemption during canary runs.
